meta.title: The Emptiest Spot in the Sky

scenes.title: The Emptiest Spot in the Sky
scenes.tagline: the photograph that changed how we see the universe
scenes.narration: In 1995, a team of astronomers made a bet that almost nobody understood.
Near the Big Dipper, they chose a patch of sky that looked completely empty.

lines: A patch the size of a tennis ball,
scenes.narration: A patch the size of a tennis ball, seen from a hundred metres away.

scenes.label: 342 exposures of one ==empty== patch
scenes.narration: Then they pointed the Hubble Space Telescope at it, and stared. For ten straight days. Three hundred and forty two exposures.

scenes.title: It wasn't empty.
scenes.narration: When the image came back, it wasn't empty.

scenes.headline: Almost every dot is a galaxy.
scenes.sub: About 3,000 of them, in one tiny patch of sky.
scenes.narration: Almost every point of light is a galaxy. About three thousand of them, each one holding billions of stars.
Some of that light left home ten billion years ago. We are seeing galaxies as they were, when the universe was young.

scenes.headline: Look closer.
scenes.narration: One empty patch of sky. Thousands of galaxies. Now imagine the rest of it.
